extracted.intended_audience: journalists, media and the astronomical/science community
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and exemplar elements for a science press release announcing a research/technical initiative, showing what information to include and how to present significance to both media and the scientific community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise headline and lead summary
rubrics_metrics.description: The press release opens with a clear headline and immediate summary: 'Exploring the Digital Universe with Europe's Astrophysical Virtual Observatory' and an opening paragraph describing the AVO launch and its capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with a strong headline and an opening paragraph that states what is happening (the initiative/announcement), who is involved, and why it matters. The page demonstrates summarizing the project's purpose and potential for discoveries in the first paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: State the aim and significance early
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim of AVO is stated explicitly: 'The aim of AVO is to give astronomers instant access to the vast databanks now being built up by the world's observatories and forming what is in effect a "digital sky".'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the problem being solved and the significance up front so readers understand the contribution (e.g., enabling instant access to multi-wavelength archives, putting the Universe online).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain the problem/context that motivated the project
rubrics_metrics.description: The release explains the challenge: 'Modern observatories observe the sky continuously and data accumulates remorselessly... The volume and complexity of data and information available to astronomers are overwhelming.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide background context that motivates the initiative—describe the scale, growth, or limitations being addressed to justify the project's importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide concrete scientific use cases/examples
rubrics_metrics.description: The release uses concrete examples of how AVO will be used, e.g., retrieving traces of an asteroid to predict its path and pinpointing a star shortly before it exploded (supernova) to study stellar evolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include vivid, concrete examples or scenarios showing practical impact to make abstract capabilities tangible for readers and journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give project details: funding, duration, start date, and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: AVO is described as 'a three-year project, funded by the European Commission... The Commission has awarded a contract valued at EUR 4m for the project, starting on 15 November.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include essential factual details about the project (funding amount, duration, start date, and scope) so stakeholders can assess scale and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: List partners and lead organization
rubrics_metrics.description: AVO involves six partner organisations led by the European Southern Observatory (ESO) in Munich, with other partners (ESA, ASTROGRID, CDS, TERAPIX, Jodrell Bank) named explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name partner organizations and, if appropriate, indicate roles or leadership to show collaboration and credibility. Provide institutional affiliations and locations where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situate the initiative in broader/international context
rubrics_metrics.description: The release situates AVO alongside other efforts: 'The National Science Foundation in the USA has awarded $10 million... for a National Virtual Observatory (NVO). The AVO project team has formed a close alliance with the NVO.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the project relates to parallel or complementary initiatives internationally to indicate scope, interoperability, and community alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer media resources and distribution details (Note for editors)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Note for editors' specifies: 'A 13-minute background video (broadcast PAL) is available from ESO PR and the Hubble European Space Agency Information Centre... It will also be transmitted via satellite on Wednesday 12 December 2001 from 12:00 to 12:15 CET on the ESA TV Service.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accessible media resources (video, broadcast schedule, availability) and distribution channels so media can use/air materials; include format and transmission details when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide named technical and PR contacts with full contact details
rubrics_metrics.description: The release lists AVO Contacts and PR Contacts with names, institutions, phone numbers (including country codes and local dialing hints), cellular numbers when available, and e-mail addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include clearly identified contacts for both scientific/technical queries and press/media enquiries, with phone and email and 24-hr contact info if possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include links and pointers to further information and events
rubrics_metrics.description: The release supplies links: 'AVO webpage: http://www.eso.org/projects/avo/index.html' and related links for NVO and an international virtual observatory conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide URLs to project webpages, partner sites, and upcoming events or conferences for journalists and interested readers to find more details or follow developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use accessible language while conveying technical capability
rubrics_metrics.description: The text explains multi-wavelength data and technical capability in non-jargon language: e.g., 'will enable astronomers to seamlessly combine data... making observations of the Universe across the whole range of wavelengths'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write for both specialist and general audiences: explain technical concepts clearly and avoid unnecessary jargon while preserving scientific accuracy so the story is usable by a wide audience.
